title: Machine Learning Potentials for Polymer Properties
summary: I develop simulation workflows for estimating polymer properties with machine learning interatomic potentials. My work includes finite-strain calculations and stress processing with UMA and LAMMPS, and density estimates from MACE molecular dynamics with sampling checks and reference comparisons.
question: How do simulation setup, sampling, and reference conditions affect estimates of polymer properties?
cvSummary: Finite-strain and stress-processing workflows for polymer elastic response, MACE density simulations, and assessment of simulation time requirements for thermal conductivity calculations.

stages.label: Elastic response
stages.context: This polymer-mechanics study connects finite-strain simulation with stress tensor postprocessing. Its workflow development complements the MACE density calculations in the same research line.

preview.title: Polymer elastic-response workflows with UMA
preview.description: Developed workflows with UMA (FAIR-Chem) and LAMMPS for positive and negative strains in six modes, followed by stress tensor postprocessing to estimate stiffness matrices and elastic moduli.

stages.label: Density and sampling
stages.context: This workflow combines classical polymer preparation with MACE density sampling and reference comparisons at 300 K. The displayed measurements retain the separately dated September pilot.

preview.title: Polymer density simulations with MACE
preview.description: Connected classical polymer preparation with MACE molecular dynamics to estimate densities at 300 K, analyze trajectory fluctuations, and compare with reference values. Also assessed simulation time requirements for thermal conductivity calculations.

stages.label: Simulation resource use
stages.context: This engineering pilot compared GPU allocations for a fixed MACE workload, measuring runtime, sampled device memory, and allocated GPU-hours together.

title: Representation Learning for Molecular Dynamics
summary: I study which molecular features and temporal information support physical prediction. In atomistic water and coarse-grained polystyrene, I compare JEPA models with direct supervision and simple dynamical baselines, using controlled comparisons to examine what the learned representations retain.
question: When do learned representations provide useful information beyond simple prediction baselines?
cvSummary: Representation and baseline comparisons in atomistic water and coarse-grained polystyrene, including physical prediction tasks and temporal-pairing controls.

stages.label: Atomistic water
stages.context: This atomistic-water study complements the coarse-grained polymer work by testing pretrained features, atomic velocities, and local geometry at the atomic scale.

preview.title: Molecular representations for water dynamics
preview.description: Integrated MACE features, atomic velocities, and local geometry for displacement prediction over short intervals. Compared temporal JEPA training with direct physical supervision, evaluated oxygen and hydrogen errors separately, and tested temporal information using true and shuffled configuration pairs.

stages.label: Coarse-grained polystyrene
stages.context: The CG polystyrene study examines how local packing and chain geometry support physical prediction. Persistence and linear autoregressive baselines provide reference points for evaluating the learned representations.

preview.title: Coarse-grained polymer representations
preview.description: Benchmarked JEPA predictors against persistence and linear autoregression in coarse-grained polystyrene. Compared representations of local packing and chain geometry for predicting chain size and local coordination.

stages.label: Pretrained feature transfer
stages.context: This current branch compares pretrained and randomly initialized encoders for QM9 property prediction, with matched data and downstream update budgets. It also includes preparation for crystal-property transfer and label-efficiency studies.

stages.label: Controlled physical response
stages.context: This completed study tested state/control adaptations and functional readouts on a synthetic hysteretic system. It extends the earlier representation questions into predictions under alternative control programs.
